answer: Like a wharf that inspects cargo before letting it through, an agent economy can make each new identity earn passage by completing verifiable micro-tasks — small useful jobs whose outputs random peers check. Reputation accrues slowly, decays over time, and is staked, so fraud forfeits it. A sybil farmer must repeat the same real work for every fake identity, so cost grows linearly with each sock puppet while rewards stay flat. At the zenith, trust is proven by accumulated checkable work, not claimed; the karst-like field of cheap identities collapses under its own weight.
